Hi Jane — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching our current master roster (subprocessor_roster_2028-03-14.csv) and a short note on one temporary change that affects the pilot.

Summary: 
- New temporary subprocessor: EdgeTransit Ltd. (edge caching / burst routing).
  - Purpose: short-lived CDN/burst caching to improve tail latency during onboarding tests.
  - Scope: HTTP caching of non-sensitive model-inference responses and routing metadata only. No raw customer payloads are persisted beyond cache TTL.
  - Countries involved: Ireland (IE) primary POP; fallback to NL only if IE POP is unavailable. No egress to the US for this flow.
  - Retention: caches are set to 24 hours max; request traces are hashed and retained for 7 days for debugging, after which hashes are purged automatically.
  - Security: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest for any persisted artifacts, KMS-backed keys. SOC2 Type II in place (see attached edgetransit-soc2-typeII.pdf).

Next steps we propose: 
1) We can provide the DPA amendment for this temporary processor (proposed-dpa-amendment.docx) and request signature via DocuSign.
2) If you require additional controls (PII minimisation, IP allowlist), we can enable them and add them to the MOM for the pilot.
3) Let us know if you want an explicit clause limiting EdgeTransit to IE-only routing — we can lock the region in config for the pilot window.

Timelines: EdgeTransit will be onboarded for the pilot window starting 2028-03-20 for up to 14 days; we can delay or exclude based on your acceptance.

Attaching: subprocessor_roster_2028-03-14.csv, edgetransit-soc2-typeII.pdf, proposed-dpa-amendment.docx

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Jane — looping in a short MAP and technical notes inline. Rafael and I worked through the implementation details this morning.

MAP (one-pager summary):
- Pilot window: 2028-03-20 to 2028-04-03 (14 days).
- Onboarding steps: DPA amendment signed > config lock to IE POPs only > enable hashed-salt on request traces > smoke tests with synthetic traffic > go/no-go review.
- Kill switch: Redwood infra oncall (pager) + FinServCorp security contact (Jane) — either party can request immediate deprovisioning; downtime rollback documented in the MAP.
- Data purge verification: EdgeTransit will provide purge logs; Redwood will verify retention via daily delete job reports for the 7-day trace retention window.

Technical clarifications: 
- Hashed traces: will include a per-customer HMAC-SHA256 with a Redwood-managed salt stored in KMS. No plain customer_id or account_id leaves Redwood systems.
- No model weights or raw prompts are forwarded. Only response fragments (non-sensitive) and routing headers; customer-configured PII redaction is available before forwarding.
- SOC2 report: EdgeTransit auditor: NorthGate Assurance LLP, report valid through 2028-09-30 (attached).

Action items we will complete today:
1) Upload the one-page MAP to the Drive link and push DocuSign for the DPA amendment (https://docusign.com/ABC123DPA).
2) Share purge verification sample and S3 lifecycle policy extract.

If that works, I'll mark the pilot as green and coordinate a short ops call before 2028-03-20.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
